column3: NASB renders “to register all the world” as “that a census be taken of all the inhabited earth.”
NASB follows the critical text without “wife”; “betrothed” is rendered “engaged.”
NASB has “suddenly” where the Textus Receptus has “behold”; “feared a great fear” is “were terribly frightened.”
NASB follows the critical text; “swaddled” is rendered “wrapped in cloths.”
NASB follows the critical text (“men of good will,” rendered “men with whom He is pleased”).
NASB follows the critical text without “the men”; “declaration” is rendered “thing,” and it adds “straight.”
NASB follows the critical text; “declaration” is rendered “statement.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Him”) and renders “to circumcise Him” as “before His circumcision.”
NASB puts the verse in parentheses and italicizes “firstborn”; the quotation is in capitals.
Close to the Greek; the quotation is in capitals.
